text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.6% today to close at $150.80, extending a sharp two-week rally. The move follows escalating Middle East tensions—Saudi Arabia intercepted Iranian-backed Houthi missiles and drones this week, and Brent crude oil has climbed to $116 a barrel, its highest level in six months, on concerns about potential U.S. military action against Iran. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, especially with the geopolitical risk premium now pushing oil higher.

The broader energy trade is in motion: oil prices are up roughly 7% since mid-October as investors price in regional supply disruptions and growing friction with Iran. U.S. oil is trading at $107.89 per barrel versus Brent at $115.22—a widening spread that signals particular strength in global markets where most of ConocoPhillips' production is valued, amplifying the tailwind for the stock.
